title: Variables & Syscalls
description: Linux x86-64 ELF64, NASM Intel syntax, immediate values and syscalls
theory:
## Your first steps

This course uses **NASM** with **Intel syntax** on **Linux x86-64** only. Programs are assembled to **ELF64** objects, then linked with **`ld`** (raw `_start` + syscalls) or **`gcc`** when you declare **`extern`** libc routines.

### Syscall exit (64-bit Linux)

- `rax = 60` (`sys_exit`)
- `rdi = exit code`
- `syscall`

### Syscall write

- `rax = 1` (`sys_write`)
- `rdi = fd` (1 = stdout)
- `rsi = buffer address`
- `rdx = length`
- `syscall`

### Curriculum

This slot matches the shared [LEARN-LANGUAGES/CURRICULUM.md](../../CURRICULUM.md) `variables` chapter for **Asm (Adapted)**—here the “bindings” are registers and immediates wired to syscalls.

exercises.title: Exit cleanly
exercises.description: Write a program with global `_start` that exits with status 0 using the exit syscall. It should print nothing.
exercises.starter_code:
; NASM Intel, Linux x86-64
; Exit with code 0 (no output)

global _start
section .text
_start:
    ; rax = 60 (sys_exit), rdi = 0
    ; syscall
exercises.solution:
global _start
section .text
_start:
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall

exercises.title: Write to stdout
exercises.description: Use the `write` syscall to print exactly `Hi` (two characters, no newline).
exercises.starter_code:
global _start
section .data
    msg: db 'H','i'
    len equ $ - msg
section .text
_start:
    ; rax=1 write, rdi=1 stdout, rsi=msg, rdx=len
    ; then exit 0
hints: After write, exit with `mov rax, 60` / `xor rdi, rdi` / `syscall`
exercises.solution:
global _start
section .data
    msg: db 'H', 'i'
    len equ $ - msg
section .text
_start:
    mov rax, 1
    mov rdi, 1
    mov rsi, msg
    mov rdx, len
    syscall
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall

exercises.title: Digits on stdout
exercises.description: Print exactly `42` (no newline) using one `write` syscall, then exit 0.
exercises.starter_code:
global _start
section .data
    msg: db '4','2'
    len equ $ - msg
section .text
_start:
hints: Same pattern as the previous exercise: `rax=1`, `rdi=1`, `rsi`, `rdx=len`
exercises.solution:
global _start
section .data
    msg: db '4', '2'
    len equ $ - msg
section .text
_start:
    mov rax, 1
    mov rdi, 1
    mov rsi, msg
    mov rdx, len
    syscall
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall

exercises.title: Call libc printf
exercises.description: Use **`extern printf`**, **`global main`**, and link with **gcc** (the runner detects `extern`). Print one line: `Hello from libc` followed by a newline. Expected stdout after trim is `Hello from libc` (the newline is trimmed).
exercises.starter_code:
default rel
extern printf
section .text
global main
main:
    ; align stack, then call printf with format in rdi
    ret
section .data
    fmt: db "Hello from libc", 10, 0
hints: `sub rsp, 8` before `call` helps satisfy 16-byte stack alignment on entry
`xor eax, eax` before `call printf` (AL = 0 vector regs for variadic)
exercises.solution:
default rel
extern printf
section .text
global main
main:
    sub rsp, 8
    lea rdi, [rel fmt]
    xor eax, eax
    call printf
    add rsp, 8
    xor eax, eax
    ret
section .data
fmt: db "Hello from libc", 10, 0

exercises.title: Three-byte write
exercises.description: Print exactly `Asm` (three letters, no newline) with a single `write` syscall from a `.data` buffer, then exit 0.
exercises.starter_code:
global _start
section .data
    msg: db 'A','s','m'
    mlen equ $ - msg
section .text
_start:
    ; rax=1 write stdout rsi=msg rdx=mlen then sys_exit 0
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall
exercises.solution:
global _start
section .data
    msg: db 'A', 's', 'm'
    mlen equ $ - msg
section .text
_start:
    mov rax, 1
    mov rdi, 1
    lea rsi, [rel msg]
    mov rdx, mlen
    syscall
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall
